target.title: fix(ui): keep agent avatar initials on grapheme clusters
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Control UI agent avatar fallbacks used `.slice(0, 1)` on the agent name/id.
Names starting with a flag emoji (`🇺🇸Team`) or ZWJ sequence (`👨‍💻Dev`) were
cut mid-cluster and rendered as replacement characters / incomplete glyphs.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add `resolveFallbackAvatarInitial` using `Intl.Segmenter` grapheme granularity
and use it in the three agent avatar fallback call sites. Keep the prior
locale-independent `toUpperCase()` casing contract (not `toLocaleUpperCase()`).

When `Intl.Segmenter` is unavailable, do **not** use `Array.from` / code-point
slicing (that still splits flags and ZWJ sequences). Keep ASCII alphanumerics
only and return `?` for emoji-leading labels so incomplete glyphs are never shown.

## User Impact

**Before:** Agent names beginning with multi-code-point emoji produced broken
avatar initials.

**After:** Fallback avatars keep a complete grapheme (flag / ZWJ emoji / letter)
with the same ASCII casing behavior as before. Engines without Segmenter show
`?` for emoji-leading names instead of a half-flag / half-ZWJ glyph.

## Evidence

- Changed: `ui/src/lib/agents/display.ts`, `ui/src/lib/agents/display.test.ts`,
  `ui/src/components/app-sidebar.ts`,
  `ui/src/components/app-sidebar-agent-menu.ts`,
  `ui/src/pages/agents/panels-overview.ts`,
  `ui/src/test-helpers/app-sidebar-cases/agent-menu.ts`
- Production path: sidebar agent card / agent menu / agents overview identity
  editor → `resolveFallbackAvatarInitial(label)` when no text avatar is configured
- Compatibility: ASCII initials still uppercased via `toUpperCase()`; empty
  labels become `?`; Segmenter-missing path refuses emoji clusters (`?`) rather
  than splitting them
- Visual gap: no Playwright Control UI screenshot in this update; jsdom mounts
  the same production Lit sidebar templates and asserts the avatar slot text

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

Mounted Control UI sidebar renders `🇺🇸` in the agent-chip avatar slot for
`identity.name = "🇺🇸Team"`, and menu switch rows render `🇺🇸` / `👨‍💻` for
flag- and ZWJ-leading agent names. Without Segmenter, flag/ZWJ labels become
`?` instead of incomplete glyphs.

### Canonical reachability path

Control UI agent chip / menu / overview →
`resolveAgentTextAvatar(...) ?? resolveFallbackAvatarInitial(label)` →
`.sidebar-agent-card__avatar-text` / `.sidebar-agent-section__avatar`

### Shared helper / provider constraint check

Same Segmenter primary path as `ui/src/pages/plugins/presentation.ts`
`takeGraphemes`, but avatar fallback intentionally refuses the
`Array.from`-style incomplete-cluster fallback; no new config.

### Real environment tested

Local trusted source checkout at PR head; jsdom Control UI component mount via
existing `mountSidebar` harness (same production Lit templates as the live
sidebar); Node via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs`. Playwright Control UI screenshot
not run in this pass (no secrets needed, but no focused avatar e2e exists;
jsdom caller-path proof covers the rendered avatar slots).

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/lib/agents/display.test.ts \
  -t "resolveFallbackAvatarInitial" --reporter=verbose
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/components/app-sidebar.test.ts \
  -t "complete flag and ZWJ" --reporter=verbose
```

### Evidence after fix

Helper + Segmenter-missing fallback:

```text
stdout | resolveFallbackAvatarInitial > keeps flag and ZWJ emoji clusters intact
avatar-initial proof: {"flag":"🇺🇸","zwj":"👨‍💻","ascii":"A"}

stdout | resolveFallbackAvatarInitial > avoids splitting flag/ZWJ clusters when Intl.Segmenter is unavailable
avatar-initial Segmenter-fallback proof: {"ascii":"A","flag":"?","zwj":"?"}

 ✓ resolveFallbackAvatarInitial > keeps flag and ZWJ emoji clusters intact
 ✓ resolveFallbackAvatarInitial > keeps locale-independent ASCII casing (Turkish i)
 ✓ resolveFallbackAvatarInitial > avoids splitting flag/ZWJ clusters when Intl.Segmenter is unavailable

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  3 passed | 17 skipped (20)
```

Rendered Control UI avatar slots (production Lit templates via `mountSidebar`):

```text
stdout | AppSidebar agent chip > renders complete flag and ZWJ graphemes in the agent chip avatar slot
sidebar avatar-slot proof: {"chip":"🇺🇸","flagMenu":"🇺🇸","zwjMenu":"👨‍💻"}

 ✓ AppSidebar agent chip > renders complete flag and ZWJ graphemes in the agent chip avatar slot

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 140 skipped (141)
```

### Observed result after fix

The live sidebar agent-chip and agent-menu avatar slots render complete flag
and ZWJ graphemes instead of UTF-16-sliced fragments, without changing the
prior `toUpperCase()` casing contract. The Segmenter-unavailable path no longer
uses `Array.from`, so flags/ZWJ are not shown as incomplete glyphs.

target.title: fix(nostr): strip internal tool-trace banners from outbound text
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Nostr direct messages could expose internal assistant tool-failure banners and tool-call XML instead of sending only user-visible reply text.

Related: #90684

## Why This Change Was Made

Nostr opts into the shared assistant-visible-text sanitizer through its standard outbound adapter hook. Its inbound DM reply callback also applies the same sanitizer because it delivers directly through the Nostr bus and bypasses the core outbound adapter pipeline.

The narrowed Nostr adapter type requires the sanitizer hook, preventing a later adapter refactor from silently dropping this delivery invariant while still type-checking. The direct callback suppresses trace-only output before Markdown conversion and relay delivery.

This rebase preserves current main's Nostr ingress architecture: `runPassiveAccountLifecycle`, `dispatchInboundDirectDm`, and its ingress lifecycle handoff remain intact. It does not restore the retired runtime dispatcher path.

## User Impact

Nostr recipients see intended assistant prose without internal tool traces or XML scaffolding. Ordinary prose remains unchanged, and a reply containing only internal trace content does not produce an empty DM.

## Evidence

- Standard outbound regression coverage verifies the adapter's shared sanitizer for mixed text, XML tool calls, multiline tool-response scaffolding, and ordinary prose.
- Inbound direct-reply regressions exercise the current lifecycle-aware dispatcher callback and verify mixed visible/trace content is sanitized before Markdown conversion while trace-only output invokes neither Markdown conversion nor the relay reply callback.
- Rebased exact head: `4947413d6f0e713700156323ec57948e4d0d563e`.
- Exact-head upstream CI: [success](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29684297405).

## Risk checklist

- [x] One concern, one PR: prevent internal assistant scaffolding in Nostr outbound text.
- [x] Standard outbound and inbound direct-reply bypasses both use the same shared sanitizer.
- [x] Current ingress lifecycle and dispatcher contracts are preserved.
- [x] No config/env/default surface, SDK expansion, dependency, or CHANGELOG change.
- [x] Allow edits by maintainers.

target.title: refactor: own model discovery by runtime lifecycle
target.body:
Related: #90741

## What Problem This Solves

Model catalog consumers repeatedly rebuilt auth stores, provider registries, and projected catalogs on request-time paths. That duplicated filesystem and plugin discovery across agent context, provider auth, session status, replies, cron, doctor, model listing, the TUI, and media tools, while separate caches could expose mismatched auth, registry, and catalog generations.

## Why This Change Was Made

This completes the lifecycle-owned catalog program. Gateway/config/auth publication now builds one atomic prepared model runtime generation per configured agent, synchronously stales the previous owner, and lets request paths fork mutable auth/registry state while reusing the generation's catalog snapshot. The context, provider-auth, session-status, auto-reply, cron, doctor, media-understanding, model-list, TUI, subagent spawn, PDF, and image-runtime consumers now use that prepared generation.

The request-time model discovery caches and their obsolete export paths are deleted. The released plugin SDK `loadModelCatalog` entry point remains only as a deprecated compatibility wrapper; all internal and bundled callers use the lifecycle-owned API.

Thanks to @zeroaltitude for the original performance investigation, measurements, and sponsored direction.

## User Impact

Model-aware commands and runtime paths reuse a coherent catalog snapshot instead of paying repeated discovery cost. Auth/config publication swaps the whole generation together, so callers do not observe a new auth store paired with an old registry or catalog. PDF and image sub-runs inherit the parent generation rather than rediscovering models.

Concurrent standalone activations for the same owner are serialized through a per-owner FIFO, which prevents competing direct-command generations from continually staling one another. The late-added subagent structured-output validation path also consumes the prepared catalog rather than restoring request-time discovery.

## Evidence

Node 24 benchmark, 20 batches of 25 operations (500 total):

| Path | p50 | p95 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Request-time discovery | 1027.666 us | 1094.410 us |
| Lifecycle snapshot | 3.349 us | 5.864 us |

- p50 speedup: **306.81x**
- one-time lifecycle build: **40.479 ms**
- final exact changed gate: green on Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kxwxdcjwtxe1f81f3da6njqz` ([run 29682735289](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29682735289)) across formatting, SDK API/package/surface/deprecation/boundary checks, all five TypeScript lanes, complete core/extensions/scripts lint, schema/database/media/sidecar/import-cycle/webhook/pairing guards
- post-rebase focused lifecycle, subagent, swarm, PDF/image tool, and Telegram suites: 268/268 green
- media/PDF registration and tool suites after the final model-context extraction: 153/153 green
- mandatory full-tree autoreview found and drove closure of generation, workspace, read-only identity, provider-alias, and standalone-activation lifecycle races; each follow-up patch received a fresh clean review
- packaged build was green before the final internal-only lifecycle fixes; the final exact changed gate revalidated their type, lint, formatting, SDK, and boundary surfaces

## Designed Follow-up

The Plugin SDK compatibility facade still owns process-global API-provider publication; each prepared generation snapshots it into its per-registry runtime. Moving publication ownership itself out of process-global state is a designed follow-up, intentionally outside this program.

## AI Assistance

Codex assisted with implementation, tests, review, benchmark execution, and PR drafting under maintainer direction.

target.title: Durable Core PR 4/6: persist agent-turn front doors
target.body:
## Stack Position

Durable Core PR 4/6, gated on the latest completed ClawSweeper review for PR3 #111278 (overall Gold Shrimp).

This PR targets `release/2026.7.1`, so GitHub shows the cumulative durable-core stack. The reviewable PR4-only delta is:

https://github.com/mjnkao/openclaw/compare/codex/durable-core-pr3-recovery-v5...codex/durable-core-pr4-agent-turn-v1

- Stack parent: `3c344e0a98f34dbb954275f45ca738f744aea3e7`
- Exact head: `2e95463c53aa4bd025c7702634dab684d209b85c`
- Database schema delta from PR3: none
- New configuration delta from PR3: none

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw 7.1 entry points can acknowledge agent work before durable evidence exists. During long tool work, Gateway restart can leave the caller with an uncertain outcome; the established CLI fallback or restart recovery can then run the same work again and risk duplicate side effects.

This slice persists admission, liveness, and settlement around existing agent-turn and `chat.send` front doors:

- channel reply and queued follow-up runners
- CLI Gateway path
- isolated cron execution
- Gateway `agent` RPC
- OpenAI-compatible HTTP streaming
- OpenResponses streaming
- `chat.send`

It reuses the PR2 durable tables and PR3 recovery/owner-attention substrate. It adds no generic executor, parallel worker, database table, or hidden environment activation path.

## Contract

- Persist intake before dispatch or success-shaped acceptance output.
- Await durable admission before the first OpenAI assistant chunk.
- Await durable admission before OpenResponses created/in-progress/output events.
- Fail closed in `authority` mode when intake cannot be persisted.
- Keep `observe` best effort and disabled mode database-free.
- Renew a 30-second heartbeat while a turn is active.
- Settle each turn through one fenced terminal path.
- Store message length and SHA-256 hash, not raw prompt text.
- Mark intake metadata-only and non-replayable.
- Refuse CLI embedded fallback after an uncertain Gateway result.
- Block main-session auto-resume while an open `lost_after_dispatch` fact exists.
- Deliver restart attention with tools disabled, including after persistent queue recovery.
- Keep explicit retry authority with the source owner.

## Current-Head Corrections

ClawSweeper's previous review found that both HTTP streaming paths could emit success-shaped events before asynchronous durable admission rejected. Exact head `235f75d` introduced one awaitable ingress admission boundary, preserved the same run identity and lifecycle generation, and added rejection regressions for both endpoints.

Live fault validation then found a second replay route: the durable restart wake could activate the interrupted transcript and the model could repeat a missing tool process despite the warning prompt. Exact head `2e95463` closes that route at deterministic owner boundaries:

1. Main-session restart recovery performs a read-only authority-mode uncertainty check and will not auto-resume a transcript with open side-effect uncertainty.
2. A `restart_interrupted` attention payload persists `disableTools=true`; queue recovery preserves it and the heartbeat runner removes all tools and skills for that attention turn.
3. Durable attention is classified as a real wake payload, so an empty `HEARTBEAT.md` cannot suppress the owner update.

The replay fence is independent of model strength, prompt compliance, or context-window size.

## Evidence

### Exact-head validation

Exact head `2e95463c53aa4bd025c7702634dab684d209b85c` passed:

- focused current-head matrix: 359 tests across 5 Vitest shards
- unit shard: 32 passed
- Gateway OpenAI/OpenResponses matrix: 159 passed
- infra heartbeat/system-event/session-queue shard: 96 passed
- command/fail-closed fallback shard: 37 passed
- main-session restart-recovery shard: 35 passed
- `pnpm tsgo:all`
- changed-file type-aware Oxlint
- `pnpm lint:agent:ingress-owner`
- Oxfmt on all changed files
- `git diff --check`
- exact-head `pnpm build`, reporting `OpenClaw 2026.7.1 (2e95463)`

Regression coverage proves:

- OpenAI admission failure emits no assistant success chunk.
- OpenResponses admission failure emits no created, in-progress, or output event.
- Open durable side-effect uncertainty blocks main-session auto-resume.
- Restart attention preserves `disableTools=true` through the persistent queue.
- Durable attention bypasses an empty heartbeat file without exposing tools.

### Exact-head isolated restart and no-replay trace

An isolated authority-mode Gateway used channels/bindings disabled and a private loopback endpoint.

1. A normal CLI-to-Gateway turn persisted `received -> running -> succeeded`.
2. A second turn appended one line to an isolated side-effect counter, then entered a 120-second tool wait.
3. Before shutdown it remained `running/running`, recorded a heartbeat at 30,002 ms, and the side-effect count was exactly one.
4. Gateway shutdown made the waiting CLI exit non-zero with the explicit uncertain-outcome message; embedded fallback did not run.
5. Restart against the same SQLite state produced exactly one `lost/lost` turn, one open `lost_after_dispatch` fact, and one `restart_interrupted` wake.
6. The attached attention turn ran without tools and ACKed the wake in one attempt.
7. The side-effect count remained one and the transcript contained exactly one `exec` call and zero `process` calls.
8. A separate post-restart CLI turn succeeded normally.
9. A third boot changed only the Gateway startup count.

Stable counts across the third boot:

```text
lost_agent_turns=1
succeeded_agent_turns=3
uncertainty_facts=1
open_uncertainty_facts=1
wake_obligations=1
acked_wakes=1
wake_attempts=1
side_effect_count=1
transcript_exec_calls=1
```

The isolated durable database contained zero raw proof-marker occurrences in `metadata_json`; records retained bounded lengths and hashes only.

## Boundary

This PR does not claim arbitrary tool-process resumption, automatic replay from metadata-only intake, exactly-once external effects, or external-channel delivery. Durable core records uncertain effects, prevents automatic replay, and routes owner attention; reconciliation or explicit retry remains an owner decision.

PR5 remains the subagent lifecycle/restart bridge. PR6 remains the read-only operational API/CLI surface.

This PR is AI-assisted. The implementation and proof were manually reviewed against the owner-authority, admission, recovery, replay, privacy, and disabled-mode boundaries above.

The Control UI mock has limited curated chat state for design QA, so reviewers have to rely on ad hoc sessions when checking empty chat, longer transcripts, markdown rendering, code blocks, tables, warnings, and recoverable error copy.

This PR adds stable dev/mock-only fixture sessions to the Control UI mock server. The proposed fixtures cover a New session empty state, a coding session, a response-shape showcase, and a markdown showcase without changing production gateway or session APIs.

There is no production user-facing behavior change. Developers and designers can load stable mock chat sessions for future Control UI visual review.

target.title: fix(microsoft-foundry): bound az subprocess lifetime on exec timeout
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`execFileSync` default `killSignal` is `SIGTERM`. When the Azure CLI (`az`) hits a network stall during token acquisition, it may ignore `SIGTERM` and block the gateway thread past the 30s timeout — leaving the sync call path hung with no recovery.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adding `killSignal: "SIGKILL"` to the `execFileSync` call ensures the `az` subprocess is forcefully terminated when the 30s timeout fires.

The async counterpart `execAzAsync` calls `runExec` (from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/process-runtime`), not the Node.js built-in `execFile`. `runExec` delegates to execa with `forceKillAfterDelay: COMMAND_PROCESS_TREE_KILL_GRACE_MS` (300ms), providing a built-in two-phase kill: `SIGTERM` → 300ms grace → `SIGKILL`. Source: `src/process/exec.ts:50-63`, `src/process/exec-spawn.ts:7`.

## Evidence Map

| Layer | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Changed surface** | `execAz` in `extensions/microsoft-foundry/cli.ts:47-58` — one line |
| **Node.js contract** | `execFileSync` default `killSignal` is `SIGTERM` (Node.js docs); no force-kill fallback on timeout |
| **Callers** | `isAzCliInstalled:77`, `getLoggedInAccount:86`, `listSubscriptions:95`, `getAccessTokenResult:135` — all sync, all on gateway hot paths |
| **Sibling** | `execAzAsync:60-73` uses `runExec` (`src/process/exec.ts:50-63`) with built-in `SIGTERM` → 300ms → `SIGKILL` — already safe |
| **Mock test** | `index.test.ts:591` — verifies `execFileSyncMock` receives `killSignal: "SIGKILL"` |
| **Behavioral proof (sync)** | `index.test.ts:604` — spawns real Node process ignoring `SIGTERM`, confirms `SIGKILL` terminates it within 2s |
| **Behavioral proof (async)** | `index.test.ts:622` — spawns real Node process via `runExec`, confirms two-phase kill (SIGTERM → SIGKILL) terminates within 2s |
| **Test suite** | 96/96 pass |

## User Impact

- Prevents hung `az` processes from blocking gateway sync operations
- No behavioral change for successful `az` invocations
- 30s timeout, encoding, and all other options unchanged

Related: #104485

## What Problem This Solves

Ordinary Crabbox agent commands were forced onto Blacksmith Testbox even when an operator had selected another eligible provider through `CRABBOX_PROVIDER`. That made machine-local provider preferences ineffective and could also cause local-container execution to be described as remote/Testbox proof.

## Why This Change Was Made

Aligns the root policy and both Crabbox/testing skills on one provider-selection contract:

1. Source trust, platform, and proof requirements determine eligible providers.
2. An explicit eligible provider requested by the user wins.
3. Ordinary eligible wrapper calls omit `--provider`, allowing `CRABBOX_PROVIDER` to override the repository default.
4. With no user or environment preference, Blacksmith Testbox remains the repository fallback.

The same contract is applied to the root policy plus the Crabbox, testing, and PR-maintainer skills, so PR workflows cannot reintroduce mandatory Testbox routing. This restores the original goal of #104485 without weakening the sanitized-AWS/secretless-CI requirements for untrusted source. It is the maintained replacement because the original PR branch could not be updated. Original contributor: @hxy91819.

## User Impact

Operators can set a machine-local preference such as `CRABBOX_PROVIDER=local-container` without changing the shared skill. AWS or another eligible provider can be selected the same way. Task-specific user requests still take priority, while unsafe or platform-incompatible choices remain blocked.

## Evidence

- Current head: `32452922d779597437621cdf63fb02d740b49837`.
- Dependency contract checked in Crabbox source: config files load before environment overrides, `CRABBOX_PROVIDER` overrides the configured provider, and an explicit CLI `--provider` remains the final override.

target.title: fix(memory-lancedb): make table initialization atomic
target.body:
Closes #105680

## What Problem This Solves

The bundled LanceDB memory plugin checked whether the `memories` table existed and then created it in a separate operation. Two OpenClaw processes initializing the same database could both observe the table as absent, race during creation, and fail startup with a duplicate-create error.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the existing fast path for an already-present table, but make the absent-table path use the LanceDB 0.30.0 atomic `existOk` create mode. This keeps concurrency ownership in the database dependency, avoids a filesystem lock that would not fit remote storage URIs, and keeps schema-row cleanup idempotent.

The regression test starts six independent Node processes against one fresh LanceDB directory and requires every process to complete initialization successfully. The same scenario fails against the previous implementation.

LanceDB documents that `existOk: true` suppresses the existing-table error in create mode and ignores the losing caller supplied data: https://lancedb.github.io/lancedb/js/interfaces/CreateTableOptions/

## User Impact

Gateway and worker processes can initialize the same memory-lancedb store concurrently without intermittent duplicate-create startup failures.

## Evidence

Final-head validation:

- Candidate head: `4e1bc84e3e1`; rebased onto `origin/main` at `652266b8b6c`.
- Production diff after the current TypeScript LOC ratchet: `12 additions / 13 deletions`; the legacy production file no longer grows.

### Standalone concurrent-process behavior proof

Environment: macOS arm64, Node 24.15.0, exact `@lancedb/lancedb@0.30.0`, one fresh temporary local LanceDB directory. This proof ran outside Vitest. The temporary driver started six independent Node processes; each imported the production `extensions/memory-lancedb/index.ts` module and called `testing.createMemoryDb(dbPath, 4).count()`.

Pre-fix control: the same final-head snapshot with only `{ existOk: true }` removed while retaining the test access hook:

```text
initializer 2: failed (1)
initializer 3: failed (1)
initializer 4: failed (1)
initializer 5: failed (1)
initializer 1: failed (1)
initializer 6: ok
Error: Table memories already exists
before_exit=1
```

Final head:

```text
initializer 5: ok
initializer 1: ok
initializer 3: ok
initializer 6: ok
initializer 4: ok
initializer 2: ok
tables: memories
rows: 0
after_exit=0
```

The final table is usable, all six initializers return successfully, and the temporary schema row is removed.

### Tests and gates

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-lancedb/index.test.ts extensions/memory-lancedb/memory-lancedb.concurrent.test.ts` under Node 24.15.0 — 2 files and 126 tests passed.
- `check:changed` passed conflict markers, the TypeScript LOC ratchet, attributions, extension export guards, duplicate coverage, dependency pins, and formatting. Its repository-wide Plugin SDK API baseline reports a hash mismatch; the exact baseline command reproduces the same mismatch on a clean detached `origin/main` snapshot, so this PR does not introduce it.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` — passed.
- Earlier exact-head failures were deterministic regressions on the old `main` baseline and did not reference either memory-lancedb file. The current `main` repair at [`2c95bd2387c`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/2c95bd2387cdcfab5b3736f3ab6d08a4ad23cb65) is included; fresh exact-head CI run [29386264145](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29386264145) passed with 46 checks green, including `openclaw/ci-gate`.

Remote Testbox delegation was unavailable because the installed Crabbox binary is 0.16.0 while the current flow requires 0.22.0 or newer. The proof above is secretless local execution, and GitHub CI remains the remote verification lane.

This supersedes #72748. That PR also carried QMD watcher changes that were independently resolved upstream by #81802 (`watch-settle.ts`), so the surviving value was just this wording alignment. Splitting it out as a small, behavior-neutral PR for easier review.

## Summary

- remove the `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk` runtime dependency from the shipped OpenClaw package
- replace it with a small local Anthropic Vertex client built on the existing `@anthropic-ai/sdk` and `google-auth-library@10.6.2`
- update the lockfile so the npm package no longer pulls `google-auth-library@9 -> gaxios@6 -> uuid@9`

## Why

`openclaw@2026.5.2-beta.1` introduced a clean npm audit regression for consumers: `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk@0.16.0` depends on `google-auth-library@^9.4.2`, which resolves to `gaxios@6.7.1` and `uuid@9.0.1`. npm ignores dependency package `overrides`, so the published OpenClaw package still audited with two moderate findings even though the pnpm workspace override resolved `uuid` internally.

## Validation

- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`
- `pnpm exec vitest run extensions/anthropic-vertex`
- `pnpm exec oxlint extensions/anthropic-vertex/stream-runtime.ts`
- `pnpm audit --prod --json` reports 0 vulnerabilities
- packed this branch with `npm pack`, installed the tarball into a fresh npm project, and verified `npm audit --omit=dev --json` reports 0 vulnerabilities
- tarball install dependency tree no longer contains `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk`, `google-auth-library@9`, `gaxios@6`, or `uuid@9`
